title: On-Demand Video Streaming Platform
summary: Design a video platform where creators upload long videos that are processed into multiple qualities and streamed smoothly to millions of concurrent viewers on any network.
statement:
You are designing **an on-demand video platform** — think of a mid-sized competitor to the big video sites. Creators upload videos; viewers watch them on phones, laptops and smart TVs.

**Creators**
- Upload videos of up to 20 GB and 4 hours, often over home or mobile connections. If the connection drops halfway, the upload should continue where it stopped instead of starting over.
- Add a title, description and thumbnail, and choose public, unlisted or private visibility.
- Follow processing progress and see each video's view count.

**Viewers**
- Open a video page and start watching within a couple of seconds.
- Get the best quality their screen and network can sustain, from 240p up to 4K. Quality adapts automatically when the network changes (e.g. walking from Wi-Fi onto a train) instead of stalling.
- Seek anywhere in the video and resume on another device where they left off.

**Clarifications from the interviewer**
- A newly uploaded video should become watchable at up to 720p quickly; 1080p and 4K versions can follow later.
- Popularity is extremely skewed: a small fraction of videos gets most of the views, and most videos are rarely watched after their first week.
- Viewers are concentrated in North America, Europe, India and Southeast Asia, each with its own evening peak.
- Delivery bandwidth is the biggest line item in the budget, followed by storage.
- Private videos must not be playable by someone who merely obtains a media URL from another user.

Cover requirements, estimates, APIs, data model and architecture for both the upload/processing path and the playback path, then go deep on the hardest parts.
scaleHints: 100M DAU watching ~40 minutes a day → ~2.8M concurrent streams on average, ~6M at peak
Average delivered bitrate ~3 Mbps → peak egress of roughly 18 Tbps
100K new uploads per day, averaging 8 minutes and ~600 MB per source file (~60 TB/day of originals)
95% of videos up to 20 minutes long must be playable at 720p within 10 minutes of the upload completing
Playback start p95 under 2 s; rebuffering under 1% of watch time
The top 1% of videos receive ~70% of views; the long tail is rarely watched after its first week
constraints: Original uploads are kept so videos can be re-encoded for new formats later
Playback availability 99.95%; uploads and processing may slow down but an acknowledged upload is never lost
Private and unlisted media require short-lived, per-viewer access
Storage and bandwidth spend must be justified — hot and cold videos should not be treated the same
outOfScope: Recommendations, search and the home page
Comments, likes, subscriptions, ads and creator monetisation
DRM licensing, copyright matching and content moderation

keyFunctionalRequirements: Resumable, chunked upload of large files plus metadata (title, description, visibility, thumbnail)
Processing: transcode into a ladder of resolutions/bitrates, generate thumbnails, package for adaptive streaming, report progress
Playback via manifests and segments with adaptive bitrate and seeking
Watch progress and resume across devices
keyNonFunctionalRequirements: ~6M concurrent streams and ~18 Tbps peak egress served close to viewers
Fast start (< 2 s p95) and < 1% rebuffering
Processing SLO: 720p playable within 10 min for videos ≤ 20 min, with horizontally scalable workers
Durability of originals and renditions; 99.95% playback availability
Cost efficiency for ~60 TB/day of new originals and for delivery bandwidth
coreEntities: Video: video_id, owner_id, title, description, visibility, status (uploading/processing/ready/failed), duration, created_at
UploadSession: upload_id, video_id, total_size, received parts/offsets, expires_at
Rendition: video_id, resolution, bitrate, codec, manifest/segment location, status
TranscodeTask: task_id, video_id, chunk range, rendition, state, attempts
keyComponents: Upload service issuing resumable, chunked upload sessions straight to object storage (pre-signed URLs)
Object storage for originals and encoded segments, with lifecycle tiering
Processing orchestrator that splits videos into chunks and schedules a DAG of transcode/thumbnail/packaging tasks
Autoscaled transcoding workers consuming a durable job queue, with retries
Metadata service and database for videos, renditions and status
Playback service that authorises viewers and returns manifests with signed URLs
CDN/edge caches with an origin shield delivering segments
deepDiveTopics: Parallel transcoding: splitting on keyframes, per-rendition tasks, stitching, retries, prioritising the 720p rendition
Adaptive bitrate streaming (HLS/DASH): encoding ladder, segment length trade-offs (startup vs efficiency), manifests
Edge delivery for head vs long-tail content: hit ratio, origin shield, pre-positioning popular videos, egress cost
Storage tiering: hot/warm/cold lifecycle, dropping rarely watched high-bitrate renditions or encoding them on demand
Protecting private videos with short-lived signed URLs/tokens validated at the edge
View counting at scale: batched events, dedup, approximate real-time counts
commonPitfalls: Streaming video bytes through application servers
Transcoding inside the upload request, or sequentially on one machine
Serving a single bitrate, so viewers on weak networks stall
Ignoring the egress estimate and treating delivery as an afterthought
Updating a database row on every view
Single-shot uploads with no resume for multi-gigabyte files
